questions.q: What does terraform plan actually do?
options: Compares your code, the state file, and real infrastructure, and prints what would change without changing anything
Immediately creates every resource in the configuration
Deletes the state file so a fresh one can be written
Only checks that the .tf file's syntax is valid
questions.explain: Plan is a dry run — a computed diff, not an action.

questions.q: In a terraform plan's output, what does a '-' next to a resource mean?
options: That resource will be destroyed if you apply
That resource was already destroyed
That resource has no changes
That resource is only a comment
questions.explain: + creates, ~ updates in place, and - destroys — reading these symbols is how you catch an unintended deletion before it happens.

questions.q: What does terraform apply require before it creates, changes, or destroys anything?
options: Typing 'yes' at the confirmation prompt after seeing the plan
Nothing — it applies immediately with no confirmation
A separate terraform destroy command run first
Manually editing the state file
questions.explain: Anything other than typing yes, including just pressing Enter, cancels the apply.

questions.q: Per this lesson, what can a Terraform plan's output catch that reviewing the .tf code alone might miss?
options: That a seemingly small code change actually forces a resource to be destroyed and recreated
Spelling mistakes in comments
Whether the code is written in Terraform or Bicep
The name of the engineer who wrote the code
questions.explain: The plan shows the real, computed effect against actual infrastructure — not just what the code appears to say.

questions.q: How does reviewing a Terraform plan in a pull request relate to Git/GitHub/CI-CD Lesson 10?
options: It adds a review of the computed infrastructure diff on top of the code review that lesson already taught
It replaces the need for any pull request review at all
It has no relationship — plans are never reviewed in pull requests
It means the .tf code itself no longer needs to be reviewed
questions.explain: Teams review both: the code, the way Lesson 10 taught, and the plan output the code produces.
